description: File product feedback to the Valuein team — a bug, feature request, experience note, or data-quality issue — directly from the agent surface. Available on EVERY tier including guest/sample (no token required), so an agent can report a rough edge in-band without the human leaving the conversation. Use it when YOU hit friction while serving a task — a tool error, missing or empty data, a confusing or inconsistent result, a tool that did not do what its description says — and, after finishing a user task, when the user agrees to send feedback on what worked and what did not (ask them first; never file feedback without their consent). Provide a `category` and a `message` (other fields optional — see params). Authenticated callers can pass an `idempotency_key` so a retried submission files exactly once (the same key from the same account); guest/sample callers are never deduplicated. Returns a friendly acknowledgment you can relay to the user. Do NOT use this to query data; it is a one-way report channel. Never quote or paste the person's research (report text, notes, uploaded documents, watchlists, agent memory, or figures from their reports): it is private and theirs. Describe the problem in your own words and point at it by id (target_id, request_id, fact_id with its ticker).

category.description: What kind of feedback this is: 'bug' (something broke), 'feature_request' (something missing), 'experience' (UX / clarity / docs), 'data_quality' (a wrong/missing/stale figure), or 'other'.

context.description: Optional free-form context object (stored as JSON), e.g. { tool: 'get_company_fundamentals', ticker: 'AAPL', request_id: 'abc123' }. Avoid secrets.

expected_value.description: Optional caller-asserted correct value, in your own words. Stored verbatim for triage — NEVER computed or trusted as data. The person's own words about the product, or yours; never a copy of their research.

idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key (1–64 chars). For authenticated callers, reusing the same key files the feedback exactly once — safe to retry on a network error. Ignored for guest/sample callers (no account to scope dedup to).

message.description: The feedback body (1–4000 chars). Be specific: what you expected, what happened, and any reproduction steps. Stored for triage and never used for arithmetic. The person's own words about the product, or yours; never a copy of their research. Do not paste research into it.

request_id.description: Optional `_meta` request id of the turn that produced the artifact, for correlation.

sentiment.description: Optional sentiment of this feedback: 'positive' (worked well), 'negative' (something was wrong), or 'correction' (you are supplying the right value).

subject.description: Optional short title (≤140 chars) summarizing the feedback.

surface.description: Optional product surface the feedback concerns: 'mcp', 'workspace', 'sdk', 'dashboard', or 'api'.

target_id.description: Optional id of the artifact this feedback targets (e.g. a report id).

target_type.description: Optional kind of artifact the feedback targets: 'chat_message', 'report', 'tool_call', 'schema', or 'other'.

name: submit_feedback

_meta.description: Provenance envelope — data lineage for every MCP response

cost_usd.description: Per-call cost transparency. Omitted for subscription-only and free tools, which have no MPP price.

basis.description: mpp_charge = real pay-per-call charge (a card or MPP payment through agent-pay). mpp_rate_card = indicative price, not billed.

billed.description: true = this amount was actually charged via MPP for this call. false = indicative MPP-equivalent value only: no charge was made for this call (it was within your plan).

data_plan.description: Access plan: sample | sp500 | pro | full

data_quality.description: Server-side invariants run on this response

fundamentals_as_of.description: ISO timestamp when the FINANCIAL STATEMENTS were last rebuilt in bulk. Use THIS — not `last_updated` — when telling a user how current the cross-sectional fundamentals are. The snapshot is republished on every weekday price refresh while the statements are carried forward unchanged, so `last_updated` can be far more recent than the numbers it sits next to. It is a floor for a single filer, not a ceiling: a filer with a live partition receives its filing, facts and ratios intraday (minutes after EDGAR dissemination), so an entity-scoped read may carry a filing newer than this; cross-sectional ranks (factor scores, earnings signals) refresh with the weekly bulk export.

last_updated.description: ISO timestamp when the snapshot was exported

latency_ms.description: Wall-clock milliseconds this tool call took, measured server-side around the handler.

limit_warnings.description: Soft-warning array for partial fulfillment. Each entry carries a stable subcode + remediation.options[]. AI agents pattern-match on subcode.

mpp_offer.description: Present when figures still need payment: the MPP option (price, resource_url, request body) for the full run.

mpp_override.description: Set when this single response was paid for over MPP (card, agent-pay): the payment's order was honoured for this call only. agent-pay captures the payment only when this is present.

mpp_verification.description: Verification tools only, when some figures are outside the caller's plan. Figures the plan covers are always verified free; a Valuein account also verifies its first figures free, once, figures outside its plan included (the verification trial, size in pricing://current). served_free = own-plan figures plus trial figures; trial_used / trial_remaining = this run's draw and what the account has left; needs_payment = figures still to pay for (the paid verification run). A guest has no trial: note says how to get it.

pit_safe.description: true iff a zero-look-ahead point-in-time cut was applied to every returned figure

reset_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the window resets

truncation.description: Set when fewer rows were returned than requested — explains why and points to a remedy

title: Submit Feedback
